title: The orchestrator runs ticfac, not a harness on a skill loop
description:
ticks-orchestrator today clones the repo at a SHA, verifies tk, provisions, runs the repository's [environment.commands] pre-flight, exports TK_ACTOR=cloud:orchestrator, and then execs a HEADLESS HARNESS on the ticks skill loop - a model deciding control flow.

Replace that last step with 'ticfac run-epic'. Everything before it stays: the clone, the preflight, the actor, and the RUN KEEPER, which already pushes the run branch as soon as there is anything on it and heartbeats on a timer. That keeper is why committed work already outlives the container.

Keep determinism. EpicReconcilerWorkflow's real improvement over the original design was replacing a model-driven orchestration loop with code; this tick keeps that and only moves where the code runs. Do not regress to 'an agent follows a skill loop'.

ticfac needs what a local run needs: a GITHUB_TOKEN for the forge surface, the profiles directory, and ticfac-exec-subprocess beside the binary (the run refuses to start without it, correctly). The executor is local-subprocess: ticfac implements only local-subprocess and herdr, and 'cloudflare-sandbox' is a reserved name in runstate.Executors with no implementation. So workers are processes in this container with their own worktrees - exactly what a local run does, and what the operator asked for: one filesystem, one git repo, a PR at the end.

Watch: standard-3 is 2 vCPU / 8 GiB / 16 GB disk, and the per-tick gate is the CPU-heavy part. Measure what max_parallel this container can actually carry rather than inheriting the local number.
notes:
2026-09-21 19:01 - The acceptance asks for the MEASURED max_parallel a standard-3 container sustains, and that is not recorded yet - it needs a real cloud run on that instance type, not a local fixture. Do not close hn0 on the PR alone; the number is the half of the acceptance that only the deployed factory can answer.

Two bugs the container run found that nothing else would have:

1. --base needs the base branch FETCHED, not just named. 'HEAD' was one problem (udu), but the remote's default branch alone was still not enough: clone_at_sha is a git init plus a fetch of one SHA, so the checkout holds the submitted commit and no branch refs at all, and 'git rev-parse main^{commit}' fails - rev-parse does not DWIM to refs/remotes/origin/main the way checkout does. The boot now resolves the default branch from origin/HEAD, else ls-remote --symref, else main with a warning, and fetches it into the checkout. A failed fetch is a stop.

2. The claude CLI refuses '--permission-mode bypassPermissions' under root - 'cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons' - and the container is root. Every ticfac worker carries that flag (internal/runconfig/kinds.go), so every dispatch would have died on a message about privileges and nothing about the run. The boot exports IS_SANDBOX=1, which is the condition's own name and is TRUE here: a disposable container with an ephemeral disk. ticks never met this because its default kind is omp, which has no such check.

Also found, filed separately: bkj (the ticfac pins sit at the top of the staged Dockerfile and bust the whole image cache, ~20 min per iteration) and r9p (run-workflow.test.ts times out intermittently; likely deleted by mn7 anyway).

And a third worth knowing: ticfac's forge surface parses the origin URL as a GitHub slug (internal/cli/forge.go -> forge.ParseRepo), so a deployment pointing TICKS_REPO_URL at the factory's own git door rather than github.com is refused at startup for a repo declaring the PR + CI rule.
acceptance_criteria: A cloud run's orchestrator container runs an epic to completion through ticfac with the local-subprocess executor, pushing the epic branch and leaving a PR, with no model deciding control flow; and the measured max_parallel this instance type sustains is recorded
